summary: iter-12 frontend UX (session_revoked notice) tested. T1-T4 PASS (manual sessionStorage flag drives login-notice, flag is consumed, no stale, invalid-creds keeps showing login-error). T5 FAIL: when /auth/me actually returns 401 detail=session_revoked, the user lands on /login WITHOUT data-testid='login-notice' visible — because api.js fires window.location.href='/login' AFTER react-router has already redirected the user and Login.jsx has already consumed sessionStorage['sc_logout_reason']; the subsequent hard reload mounts a fresh /login whose useEffect sees an empty sessionStorage. iter-9/10/11 regressions could NOT be re-exercised: in this preview the /api/* ingress is returning 404 'Not Found' for real auth (independent of code under test) so login with the seeded credentials still fails before reaching the admin pages.

critical.issue: Returns HTTP 404 'Not Found' (proxy not forwarding to network-pay-1.emergent.host). Blocks every real-auth regression test. Same infra issue flagged in iter-11.

ui_bugs.issue: On a real 401 with detail=session_revoked, the user never sees data-testid='login-notice'. Sequence (verified via TEST_HOOK on sessionStorage.setItem/removeItem): (a) interceptor sets sc_logout_reason='session_revoked' AND schedules window.location.href='/login'; (b) AuthProvider state flips to unauthenticated, react-router (PrivateRoute) navigates to /login WITHOUT a hard reload, Login.jsx mounts, useEffect reads the flag, sets notice state, removes the flag; (c) the queued window.location.href fires a HARD page reload; (d) fresh Login.jsx mounts, useEffect reads empty sessionStorage, notice is NEVER shown to the user. Net: the entire UX banner — the only thing this iteration ships — is invisible in the bug scenario it was built for.

integration_issues.issue: Race between react-router redirect (PrivateRoute) and the hard reload triggered by api.js (window.location.href='/login'). The hard reload wins the timing, but Login already consumed the sessionStorage flag during the brief react-router-only render. The notice flashes for <16ms (one frame) before being wiped.

action_items: Fix the race in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js: do NOT use window.location.href='/login' for the soft-logout path when the SPA can already react-router-navigate via the sc:unauthorized event. Option A: drop the hard redirect entirely and let AuthProvider + PrivateRoute handle the navigation (the CustomEvent is already dispatched). Option B (lower-risk): keep the hard reload but set the sessionStorage flag with a TTL/once-flag and have Login.jsx clear it ONLY when it actually renders the notice paint (e.g. inside a setTimeout(0) after setState) — but the cleanest fix is Option A.

Alternatively, persist the reason in localStorage instead of sessionStorage and have Login.jsx remove it after the notice has been displayed for at least 1s (e.g. via a setTimeout in the same useEffect). That survives both the react-router mount AND the subsequent hard reload.

Independent: restore /api/* proxy on slang-commerce.preview.emergentagent.com so real-auth regression (iter-9/10/11 system-wallet, shop-layout, products extras, header-cart/header-wishlist) can be re-exercised. Currently every /api/auth/login returns 404 in the preview ingress.
critical_code_review_comments: api.js line 84-86 hard-redirects via window.location.href even though clearTokens() + the CustomEvent already cause AuthProvider+PrivateRoute to navigate. Two redirect paths racing = the bug above. The hard reload is also semantically wrong for an SPA — it discards all in-memory React state including the notice we JUST tried to surface.

Login.jsx useEffect calls sessionStorage.removeItem immediately on first read. That makes the flag single-shot ACROSS the entire navigation chain — so if Login mounts twice (react-router mount, then hard-reload mount) only the FIRST mount sees the flag. Either keep the flag until the user submits/leaves /login, or use a paint-confirmed removal (requestAnimationFrame).

api.js line 78 only checks detail==='session_revoked'. Backend may also return variants like 'session revoked' or 'SESSION_REVOKED' from middleware. Consider a case-insensitive contains-check or matching a small set of known reasons.
Cosmetics: the notice text says 'one active session per account'. Once the backend is fixed to allow multi-session (the actual user complaint), this copy needs to come down or it will mislead users.

Login.jsx error.response.data could also expose detail==='session_revoked' from a direct login response (e.g., 'your account is already signed in elsewhere — sign out there first'). Currently that path goes into the generic error banner, not the friendly notice.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce the race with this exact recipe (no real backend needed): (1) await page.route('**/api/auth/me', r => r.fulfill({status:401, headers:{'content-type':'application/json'}, body:'{"detail":"session_revoked"}'})). (2) await page.add_init_script monkey-patches sessionStorage.setItem/removeItem to console.log every call. (3) localStorage.setItem('sc_token','fake'). (4) goto /shop. (5) Observe console: you will see setItem sc_logout_reason → removeItem sc_logout_reason → (page reload) → no notice. After the main agent fixes api.js to NOT hard-reload (or persists the flag past one mount), re-run and assert data-testid='login-notice' is visible AND remains visible after a 2s wait. Also retry T6 (detail='token_expired' → redirect WITHOUT notice). Skip the iter-9/10/11 regression suite until the preview /api proxy returns to working state (login currently 404).
rca of the issue: Race condition in the session_revoked UX path. /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js sets sessionStorage['sc_logout_reason'] then unconditionally fires window.location.href='/login'. Meanwhile clearTokens() + the sc:unauthorized CustomEvent cause AuthProvider to flip to unauthenticated, PrivateRoute triggers a react-router navigate to /login, Login.jsx mounts and useEffect immediately reads + removes the sessionStorage flag (surfacing the notice via setState). One frame later the queued hard navigation actually fires — full page reload — Login.jsx remounts on a fresh DOM, sessionStorage is now empty, the notice useEffect early-exits, the user sees a blank login page with no explanation. Reproduction (verified): page.route /api/auth/me → 401 detail=session_revoked, localStorage.setItem('sc_token','x'), goto /shop. Mitigation: pick one redirect strategy in api.js (recommend dropping window.location.href and relying on the CustomEvent + AuthProvider state) OR delay/guard sessionStorage.removeItem in Login.jsx so it survives a second mount.
